author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR24056; PTN002514139 (gain of mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling, GO:0007095)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:P06493 CDK1 (cyclin dependent kinase 1)

* **Type of Issue:** Erroneous source: the fly source shows Cdk1 as the checkpoint's target, not a participant, and the mouse source's abstract does not mention Cdk1.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


**Related tracker issue:** [geneontology/go-annotation#4146](https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/4146) (2022): another term, RNA polymerase II CTD heptapeptide repeat kinase activity, was propagated from this gain node (PTN002514139) to CDK1 on a single annotation, and was restricted to the appropriate nodes.

*CDK1 is the target that this checkpoint inhibits, not a component of it, and the fly source annotation bears this out (see the suggested change). Of its two opposing annotations, only the first (positive regulation of G2/M transition, [PMID:24746669](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24746669/)) conflicts directly; the second (positive regulation of mitotic sister chromatid segregation, [PMID:26829474](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26829474/)) conflicts only through the broad ancestor mitotic cell cycle.*

**Inherited:** CDK1 `involved_in` *mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling* ([GO:0007095](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0007095))

- **Gain:** PTN002514139 (speciation, Eukaryota; human genes below: CDK1), dated 2020-02-27.
- **Evidence genes (2):** Cdk1 (DROME), Cdk1 (MOUSE).
- **Relation to CDK1:** orthologs: Cdk1 (DROME), Cdk1 (MOUSE).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** none.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** same annotation, from PTN002514139.

**CDK1's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling*: 2 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *positive regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle* ([GO:0010971](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0010971)): [PMID:24746669](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24746669/) (IMP)
- *positive regulation of mitotic sister chromatid segregation* ([GO:0062033](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0062033)): [PMID:26829474](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26829474/) (IDA)

**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 18 sentences mention CDK1 together with *G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle*. By cue words, 9 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 2 agree.

> Consequently, CDK1/2 are hyper-phosphorylated and become inactive, which leads to intra S-phase and G2/M-checkpoint activation and cell cycle arrest48,49. **CDK1 and 2 drive S-phase progression and the G2/M cell cycle transition, but hyper-activation of CDK1/2 negatively influences DNA replication fork stability and causes premature mitotic entry50,51.** Hence, the ATR-CHK1-Cdc25-CDK1/2 pathway is necessary to regulate cell cycle progression during DNA synthesis.

— Halder S, Torrecilla I, Burkhalter MD, Popović M, Fielden J, Vaz B et al. (2019). SPRTN protease and checkpoint kinase 1 cross-activation loop safeguards DNA replication. *Nature communications*. [PMID:31316063](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31316063/).


> Because DNA damage–mediated cell cycle checkpoint progression is essential for DDR and ATM function, which are primarily activated by DSB signaling that triggers cell cycle checkpoint activation, we examined the effect of CTLA-4 on cell cycle progression. **The CDK1/cyclin B complex plays an important role in regulating the G2/M phase and facilitates the G2/M cell cycle transition (McGrath et al., 2005).** The level of the CDK1/cyclin B complex has been shown to be reduced during cell cycle arrest in the G2/M phase (Gavet and Pines, 2010).

— Yan Q, Zhang B, Ling X, Zhu B, Mei S, Yang H et al. (2022). CTLA-4 Facilitates DNA Damage-Induced Apoptosis by Interacting With PP2A. *Frontiers in cell and developmental biology*. [PMID:35281086](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35281086/).


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (2): both describe CDK1 as the target that the checkpoint inhibits. That fits the note above, not the inherited term.

> **cPAF effect on the G2–M mitotic complex The G2–M DNA damage checkpoint prevents eukaryotic cells from entering mitosis allowing for proper repair of damaged DNA, thereby preventing genomic instability.35 The G2–M mitotic transition is regulated by cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) that associates with the regulator cyclin-B1.**

— Puebla-Osorio N, Damiani E, Bover L, Ullrich SE (2015). Platelet-activating factor induces cell cycle arrest and disrupts the DNA damage response in mast cells. *Cell death & disease*. [PMID:25950475](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25950475/).


**Reasoning** (evidence-cited; verdict *error possible*, medium confidence; cause: ortholog annotation conflict): The G2 DNA damage checkpoint is defined as negatively regulating the G2/M transition, while all of CDK1's own evidence shows it driving that transition, and curated models and abstracts treat CDK1 as the kinase the checkpoint restrains rather than a part of the checkpoint signal. The term comes from fly and mouse orthologs through speciation nodes, so their experiments may reflect CDK1 being the checkpoint's target; the evidence leans against 'involved in' but does not rule it out.

- *Context:* The inherited checkpoint term is defined as detecting DNA damage and negatively regulating progression through the G2/M transition. (GO definition)
- *Against:* CDK1's own experimental annotations place it in, and as a positive regulator of, the G2/M transition, from several independent papers. ([PMID:24746669](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24746669/); [PMID:2188730](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2188730/); [PMID:2344612](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2344612/); [PMID:30139873](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30139873/); GO definition)
- *Against:* A GO-CAM of an ATR checkpoint that restricts CDK1 activation, and an abstract describing sequestration of cyclin B-CDK1 to curb its activity under replication stress, both treat CDK1 as the target that checkpoints inhibit. (gomodel:653b0ce600000721; Altmeyer 2019)
- *Against:* Literature sentences consistently describe CDK1 as driving or facilitating the G2/M transition and mitotic entry. (Halder et al. 2019; Yan et al. 2022; Ou et al. 2026; Cai et al. 2025)
- *For:* The evidence genes are direct orthologs (fly and mouse Cdk1) joined at speciation nodes, so the inheritance itself is phylogenetically sound and their experiments may have shown CDK1 regulation is required for the checkpoint. (Cdk1; PANTHER tree)
- *For:* CDK1 does take part in a DNA damage response activity (phosphorylating CtIP), showing some genuine DNA damage roles, though not checkpoint signaling per se. (gomodel:65a1f4f800001380)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Review the fly and mouse Cdk1 experimental annotations to mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling; if they only show that Cdk1 is the inhibited target (or come from mutants that escape inhibition), remove the term at PTN002514139 or add a loss for CDK1, keeping G2/M transition annotations.

*Note on the reasoning:* The claim citing [PMID:2188730](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2188730/) and [PMID:2344612](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2344612/) rests on experiments with frog MPF.

**Suggested change:**

- Remove the gain of *mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling* at PTN002514139 (Eukaryota; CDK1 is the only human gene inheriting it). Its two source annotations do not show Cdk1 taking part in the checkpoint. The fly source (IMP, [PMID:24214341](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24214341/)) uses Cdk1 that cannot be inhibited and shows that inhibitory phosphorylation of Cdk1 is needed for damage-induced G2 arrest, i.e. Cdk1 is the checkpoint's target. The mouse source (IDA, acts upstream of or within; [PMID:12937170](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12937170/)) is a study of SHP-2 whose abstract does not mention Cdk1.

### References
- Altmeyer M (2019). Cells take a break when they are TIARed. *EMBO Rep*. [PMID:30538115](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30538115/).
- Cai D, Liu C, Li H, Wang C, Bai L, Feng J et al. (2025). Foxk1 and Foxk2 promote cardiomyocyte proliferation and heart regeneration. *Nature communications*. [PMID:40128196](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40128196/).
- Halder S, Torrecilla I, Burkhalter MD, Popović M, Fielden J, Vaz B et al. (2019). SPRTN protease and checkpoint kinase 1 cross-activation loop safeguards DNA replication. *Nature communications*. [PMID:31316063](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31316063/).
- Ou Y, Lim A, Wang R, Mir N, Calsavara VF, Wang Q et al. (2026). Specific targeting of cancer cell mitochondria with a malaria drug improves pancreatic cancer outcome. *Scientific reports*. [PMID:42744873](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42744873/).
- Puebla-Osorio N, Damiani E, Bover L, Ullrich SE (2015). Platelet-activating factor induces cell cycle arrest and disrupts the DNA damage response in mast cells. *Cell death & disease*. [PMID:25950475](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25950475/).
- Yan Q, Zhang B, Ling X, Zhu B, Mei S, Yang H et al. (2022). CTLA-4 Facilitates DNA Damage-Induced Apoptosis by Interacting With PP2A. *Frontiers in cell and developmental biology*. [PMID:35281086](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35281086/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR24056: CDK1 inherits "mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint signaling", contrary to its own experimental annotations
